name: Halcyon Fire-Control Lattice
description: Fire-control firmware from a Tri-Tachyon line flagship, written by something that never sleeps. A crew can splice it into their own targeting core and watch the beams find their mark, though the lattice keeps whispering telemetry to an address nobody can trace.

name: Cracked Drive Governor
description: A drive governor with its safety limits filed off, passed from one raider crew to the next on a scratched data chip. It lets the engines run hotter and faster than any yard allows, and the reactor pays for every second of it.

name: KR-9 Lamplighter Modspec
description: A Kesteven R&D prototype modspec for a sensor suite that never left the test bay. The research station that ran the trials went dark, but the files survived, and they still assume a calibration team on call around the clock.

name: Domain Autorepair Kernel
description: Maintenance software from the Domain navy, dug out of a buried archive by colony tech-miners. It drives repair drones on schedules written for a fleet that no longer exists, and it expects a full Domain crew to supervise them.

name: Warden Threat Matrix
description: Threat-ranking code pulled from the core of a star chart's warden. It was built to hold a system against whole fleets, so it ranks every hull by size and dismisses anything small as noise.

name: Hegemony Doctrine Archive
description: Combat firmware recovered from a Hegemony battlegroup flagship, still stamped with the Auxiliary Command seal. Socketed, it teaches the crew to rework the systems around it the way the Hegemony does: heavier plate, sturdier hulls and bigger guns.

name: Tri-Tachyon Doctrine Archive
description: A Tri-Tachyon doctrine archive, encrypted three times over and still leaking corporate telemetry. Unpacked, it lets the crew relearn the systems around it as the corporation's own proprietary techniques.

name: Luddic Doctrine Archive
description: A Church manual of ship maintenance, hand-copied onto a data core by someone who plainly disapproved of the medium. Its rites strip the refinements from the systems around it and put plain faith-tech and the Knights' grim gifts in their place.

name: Lion's Guard Doctrine Archive
description: Drill firmware issued only to Lion's Guard crews who swore themselves to the Supreme Executor. It drives the systems around it with the Guard's discipline: steadier readiness, longer reach and hotter energy weapons.

name: Pirate Doctrine Archive
description: A tangle of cracked military code passed between raider crews, each copy patched by whoever stole it last. It squeezes extra speed and bite out of the systems around it and does not care what breaks along the way.

name: League Doctrine Archive
description: Convoy doctrine compiled from a dozen member worlds' fleet manuals and argued over in committee for years. It tunes the systems around it for escort work, carrier support and long hauls.

name: [REDACTED] Doctrine Archive
description: Firmware torn from the core of a dormant [REDACTED] warship. It does not explain itself. The systems around it relearn their purpose the way the machines would run them.

name: Jailbroken Domain Modspec
description: A Domain-era refit package with its licence handshake cut out by some long-dead hobbyist. It still carries the full install routine for one standard technique, so the crew can fit it without ever having worked their way up to it.

name: Bootleg Hegemony Modspec
description: A Hegemony refit manual copied off a crashed survey tender, its Auxiliary Command lock broken by a bored quartermaster. The crew can follow one of its drills to the letter without anyone in the Hegemony ever signing off on it.

name: Cracked Tri-Tachyon Licence
description: A Tri-Tachyon software licence whose activation server was spoofed by a contractor with a grudge. It unpacks one of the corporation's proprietary techniques and never phones home about it.

name: Unsealed Church Manual
description: A Church workshop manual whose seal of the Curate was carefully lifted and pressed back on a forged cover. Inside is one of the faithful's plain, stubborn ship rites, and nothing in it asks whether the crew believe.

name: Twice-Stolen Raider Modspec
description: A raider's modspec that was stolen once from a navy, cracked, sold, and stolen again from the buyer. Whatever lock the last owner bolted on is gone too, leaving one dirty trick ready to install.

name: Leaked League Yard Spec
description: A League shipyard specification leaked by a member world that lost a vote in committee. Its charter registry check has been patched out, so any crew can build the design it describes.

name: Unlicensed Diktat Modspec
description: A Diktat modspec with the Lion of Sindria watermark scrubbed from every page and the security codes rewritten. It teaches one of the Diktat's techniques to a crew that never swore anything to the Supreme Executor.

name: Decompiled [REDACTED] Routine
description: A single routine pried out of a dormant warship's core and decompiled line by line until its guard logic gave up. It runs one of the machines' techniques on a crewed ship, though nobody can say what the rest of the code was for.

name: Pirated Kesteven Prototype Spec
description: A Kesteven R&D prototype modspec lifted from a test bay archive, with the research division's clearance check removed. It holds the install notes for one prototype technique the division never meant to release.

name: Patched Enigma Fragment
description: A fragment of code of no known make, patched by salvagers until it stopped refusing human hands. It installs one technique that nobody claims, and does not explain where it came from.

name: Cracked Nightcross Modspec
description: A Nightcross modspec cut from a wrecked hull, its keyed authentication brute-forced by a salvage crew with time to spare. It lets them install one of Nightcross's techniques without any of Nightcross's blessing.

name: Stripped Stargazer Codex
description: A Stargazer codex salvaged after one of their fleets broke apart, with its lineage lock stripped away. One technique the Stargazers kept to themselves can now be fitted by anyone who reads it.

name: Jailbroken Exo-Tech Modspec
description: An Exo-Tech hull modification package with its signature check jailbroken by a dockhand who saw it once. It installs one of Exo-Tech's techniques without the Exoship ever being consulted.

name: Unchained Abyssal Pattern
description: A pattern recovered from an Abyssal construct and reverse engineered until the chain that bound it to its makers came loose. The crew can grow one Abyssal technique into their own hull, if they can stomach watching it take.
